title: max_tx_ms missing duty_permille validation
description:
File: python/src/lichen/timing/duty_cycle.py
Line: 72-82

Bug: The function accepts duty_permille without validation. Negative values produce negative transmit times, which are nonsensical.

Impact: Silent incorrect calculation. A caller passing duty_permille=-10 would receive max_tx_ms=-36000, which would fail unpredictably in downstream code expecting positive milliseconds.

Fix: Add validation:
  if duty_permille < 0:
      raise ValueError("duty_permille must be non-negative")
close_reason: Already implemented and tested on this branch: commit 5509cfc132 'fix(timing): reject negative duty permille in max_tx_ms' (and 54afd3755e for adaptive_duty_permille's density) landed the exact validation this bead requests — python/src/lichen/timing/duty_cycle.py:85-86 raises ValueError('duty_permille must be non-negative') before the arithmetic, docstring updated. Regression test pinned at python/tests/timing/test_duty_cycle.py:325-327 (pytest.raises for duty_permille=-10, the bead's exact example). Verified live: full duty-cycle test selection 132 passed. The bead was stale open work from the convergence round; closing with evidence (resurrection/stale-open pattern, like gvbc/wkya re-closes). No code change needed this round.
